brief.headline: LAUNCH's focus on high-agency technical founders with early traction, plus a 71 fit score against his Qloo audience, makes Jason Calacanis a credible investor to pitch a live-events app that turns a concert ticket into a full night out.
brief.angle: Lead with traction and the technical edge behind fanbase-matched pre-show bars, merch and rides, since LAUNCH backs pre-Series A startups that already show some traction. Position the product as the layer that extends what Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber each do for one part of the night.

name_drop.line: Your users already overlap strongly with Thumbtack's audience, so they are used to a marketplace that matches them to local services, which is the same pattern you use for bars and rides.
name_drop.name: Thumbtack

name_drop.line: Your customers show high affinity with Robinhood's audience, which tells us they are mobile-first and comfortable making repeat spending decisions in an app.
name_drop.name: Robinhood

name_drop.line: Calm's audience overlaps closely with yours, which supports building the product around a repeat, habit-driven ritual rather than a one-off event purchase.
name_drop.name: Calm

deck: Lead with traction, such as nights booked, repeat attendance or revenue per ticket, because LAUNCH's accelerator targets pre-Series A startups that already show some traction.
Show the fanbase-matching logic and how the data is built, so the technical founder profile LAUNCH looks for is visible in the deck.
Use the Qloo overlap with Thumbtack, Robinhood and Calm as audience evidence, and state the affinity scores plainly.
Address the age gap directly: your core crowd is 25 to 29 while LAUNCH's portfolio audience skews 45 to 54, so explain why your segment is the one to build for.
Frame Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber as clear reference points that show where your product fits in the night out.

openers.line: Masters of Scale covers how products scale fast, so how do you think about taking a live-events app from one city's fanbase to the next?
openers.name: Masters of Scale

openers.line: Dollar Shave Club built a subscription habit around a daily ritual, so where does a concert night fit into your users' routine?
openers.name: Dollar Shave Club

openers.line: Your bars, merch and rides look like a commerce layer on top of a ticket, so how do you think about payments and partner integrations for live events?
openers.name: Square

avoid: Do not pitch this as a consumer app without traction, since LAUNCH's accelerator and syndicate look for startups with traction and $1M+ ARR.
Do not lead with the technology alone, because LAUNCH backs high-agency technical founders but still needs proof that the business works.

Do not present Qloo affinity scores as proof of demand or as a sign of his personal tastes, since they describe the audiences of his public interests and portfolio fit, not his preferences or your revenue.
questions: What traction do you have today, such as nights booked, repeat attendance or ARR, and how is it growing month over month?
How do you keep 25 to 29 year old fans engaged after the show ends, and what does your retention look like?
Ticketmaster already owns the ticket, so why can you win the night out when venues and promoters control distribution?

picks.line: Your customers already use Uber to get to and from shows, so we'd build rides into the night out rather than compete with that habit.
Thumbtack showed how a local marketplace can turn nearby demand into repeat bookings, and we're applying that loop to venues, fans, and bars around each show.

openers.line: Ticketmaster gets fans through the door, Spotify builds the playlist, and Uber gets them home, but nothing connects the night in between, and that's the gap we're filling.
Most concert fans spend more money before and after the show than on the ticket itself, and we built an app that organizes that whole night for each fanbase.
